studies.label: Design task: sketching vs generative AI (water-saving concept design)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No uncertainty is reported for the full-sample outcome contrasts. The separate group-pair creativity t-tests use ideas as observations with no stated adjustment for randomized student groups or repeated ideas within students (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.2 (assignment) and 3.2.3 (analyzed arm counts); PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 (study total)
counts_source.quote: the design task was carried out with four student groups, randomly assigned to two predefined conditions: sketch groups A+C (n=31) and AI groups B+D (n=30).

arms.name: Sketch groups (A+C)
arms.description: Control student groups worked individually with pen and paper; devices and additional creative stimuli were unavailable (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 12, Section 5.4).

arms.name: AI groups (B+D)
arms.description: Experimental student groups worked individually using their own devices and freely chosen LLM and text-to-image tools, without prior prompting training (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 12, Section 5.4).

studies.task: Individually generate and develop concepts to promote conscious water use at home, using sketches or generative-AI tools.

ai_tool.name: Participant-selected tools: ChatGPT GPT-4o free (with fallback to a previous model) and GPT-4o Plus, DeepSeek-R1, Copilot (Azure-hosted GPT-4-class), Gemini 2.5; image tools Leonardo.AI (Phoenix), Krea.AI (Krea 1), Meshy.AI, Vizcom, PromeAI, ArtGuru, and GenCraft.
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.2.5. The study occurred in April 2025; model release years are not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or primary outcome designation is stated in the paper.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: five-point scale (1=not creative, 5=highly creative), rated by three design professors with +10 years of experience. Each rated item is an image-level concept with explanatory text. Experts agreed on anchor examples, rated individually, then re-rated in reverse order. Variations of the same AI concept were rated as one concept.

sources.quote: A total of 71 ideas for the sketch group (n=31 students) and 44 ideas for the AI groups (n=30 students) were included in the PDF document.
The study involved 61 industrial design bachelor students in their 8th semester, which is the 4th year of a total of 5 years of design studies.

estimates.notes: Full-sample condition means are reported per idea, not per participant. The analyzed participant counts accompany the included ideas in the evaluation methods. The paper does not provide a full-sample SD, SE, confidence interval, effect size, or test; no uncertainty is borrowed from the separate group-pair comparisons. Rater agreement is not uncertainty for the treatment contrast. Table medians and rating-band percentages describe this same creativity score; no SD is reconstructed from them. Abstract or discarded AI images were excluded and image variations were collapsed to concepts (PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.3).

estimates.notes: The reported numerator is 18 students. The control-arm percentage is not printed and remains null; the paper describes sketch images as more diverse (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.3). The control and total participant counts describe the full design-task comparison, not a printed control-arm repetition statistic. This is a participant-level prevalence of one repeated concept, not a pairwise similarity measure or a within-person flexibility score.

open_items: Assignment is explicitly by student group, but the paper does not identify the groups as teams, classes, or separate sessions. assignment_unit is null because the extraction vocabulary lacks an unspecified-group value; clusters_per_arm retains the confirmed grouped assignment (PDF pp. 3-4, Figure 1 and Section 3.2.2). Group formation and the randomization procedure are not described.

Full-sample creativity is summarized at the idea level, with no SD at the participant or output level and no uncertainty for the combined-arm contrast. Fluency and flexibility means also lack dispersion and inferential statistics. Precision accounting for both randomized student groups and repeated outputs is unavailable (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 4.2.1-4.2.3).

The group letters in the separate creativity tests conflict with the methods and figure caption; the standardized effect is outside its printed confidence interval. The paper supplies no correction (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1; PDF pp. 3-4, Figure 1 and Section 3.2.2).
Image-level homogenization lacks a numeric sketch-arm level and any uncertainty, so no numeric between-arm diversity effect can be recorded (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 4.2.2-4.2.3).

Condition-level category coverage is described in prose and a figure, without printed arm category totals or uncertainty in the text or a table. Figure-derived numbers are not extracted (PDF p. 8, Figure 5; PDF p. 11, Section 5.1).

The baseline AUT score-range counts are inconsistent with the stated design-task sample; the paper does not explain participant flow or the timing of randomization relative to diagnosis (PDF p. 5, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1 and 3.2.2-3.2.3). No exclusions or extra randomized participants are inferred.

The participant recruitment country is not explicitly reported. Author affiliations and the local-context example do not establish the workshop location (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1).
Release years for the named models are not reported. The dated fieldwork is not used as a model release year (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.2.5).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The complete markdown and every PDF page were read, including the references; the saved paper contains no appendix, and no supplement or public data source is identified. Only full-sample condition comparisons are extracted. All numerical statistics are transcribed without computing differences, standard deviations, confidence intervals, standardized effects, or category totals. PDF page locators are file indices plus one; no differing printed page numbering was identified. Quotes normalize whitespace only. For study totals, PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 states: "The study involved 61 industrial design bachelor students". The assignment and analyzed arm counts agree in PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.3; no design-task participant exclusions are stated. Group counts follow Figure 1 (PDF p. 3): control groups A and C and two experimental groups B and D. These are randomized clusters; students worked individually. The null assignment_unit preserves this known grouped assignment without guessing whether the groups were classes, teams, or sessions. lab_rct follows the supervised workshop with a prescribed brief and fixed task duration. Free choice of LLM and image tools is summarized as open_chat, with image generation also part of the intervention. The paper does not name another publication using these participants, a preregistration, or a primary outcome. Both across-people outcomes are retained; neither supplies a complete numeric comparison with uncertainty.
